scope: 16 standalone environment front/back inputs; built-in imagegen only; no Meshy/API/game changes

assets.details: One unfinished rectangular reinforced-concrete construction bay, with a single low roof slab, battered off-white concrete columns, an opaque lower concrete retaining wall, exposed rust-orange rebar and attached narrow scaffolding on the two visible sides. Add chipped black/yellow hazard patches at the base, a small faded A3 wall stencil, and one attached pair of square amber worklights. Fine dirty board-form concrete, rust flakes, tar streaks and irregular dark ink edges must match the reference. Keep the scaffold and lights inside the base rectangle. Close the lower access with a rusty temporary grille so the solid obstacle does not look walk-through.

One compact closed sewage pump station with weathered dark red brick, a flat tar-black slab roof and grey-green sheet-metal door. Two thick oxidized blue-grey elbow pipes and one red rusted valve wheel are attached tightly to the side and front, on a low concrete service plinth. Wet moss traces hug the base and pipe collars; faded cream P2 stencil and one small amber caged entrance lamp. Use rough stained concrete, flaking teal paint, rusty bolted pipe flanges and heavy irregular ink contours from the sewage board. No basin, water surface or surrounding catwalk.

One long narrow high-clearance industrial cargo container, closed cargo doors on its front end and corrugated blue steel sides, with rusty reddish exposed metal along the ribs and bottom corners. Heavy silver-grey locking bars, square corner castings, dented top rail, a small dirty cream A1 identification stencil and one tightly mounted amber caged lamp. The reference blue is desaturated and nearly charcoal in shadows; preserve the coarse paint flakes, salt corrosion and irregular ink-edged seams. Container only: no stacked containers, forklift, crane hook, dock, cargo piles or ground.

One closed low hospital quarantine-wing module, long rectangular flat roof with a small parapet, dirty off-white plaster interrupted by dark brown brick sections. Lower wall band of chipped pale mint square tiles, tall grimy amber windows, one sealed grey-green double isolation door with a muted green light behind its small glass panes. A short faded C1 stencil, a narrow dirty quarantine sign plate and yellow-black tape on the closed door, plus a small amber wall cage lamp. Show water streaks, chipped tile edges, taped glass cracks and rough dark ink outlines. Do not include beds, ambulance, IV bags, patients, leaking green puddles or corridor floor.

One squat closed checkpoint guardhouse: stained grey concrete and desaturated olive steel panels, flat black roof with a shallow lip, one thick steel door, a square protected front window glowing warm amber, and a tiny amber gooseneck lamp over the door. Bolted corners, chipped off-white paint, rubbed charcoal edges and rusty door hinges; a modest weathered 05 stencil and a blank narrow identification plate. Keep front and side walls solid and fit all parts within the footprint. Do not add boom gate, police van, flashing red/blue light bar, barricade line, fence or soldier.

One closed bus-depot service-bay module with a long shallow dark charcoal corrugated roof, dusty concrete sidewalls and two stout front pillars. A recessed loading face ends in a visibly closed dark olive steel shutter; warm amber pendant lights hang close to the shutter under the canopy, with a battered cream bay-number 06 plate. Brownish dirty corrugated sheet, flaking green-grey lower panel paint, battered gutter, rusted conduit and chunky irregular ink outlines from the transfer terminal reference. Roof and canopy remain within the rectangular base. No bus, cage trolley, benches, bike racks, luggage, passengers or full station.

One integrated rectangular transformer bank on a continuous low concrete plinth: two tightly coupled blue-grey steel radiator tanks, prominent vertical cooling fins, four chipped ivory ribbed ceramic bushings, thick black short cable loops clipped against the body, and a small visible copper winding sleeve. Rusty bolted covers and a tiny faded yellow high-voltage triangle, with one subdued amber pilot lamp. Preserve stained cream ceramics, dark wet fin crevices, green-grey control-box paint and heavy fine ink edges from the power substation board. Every terminal and wire stays inside the stated outer silhouette. No electric arcs, lightning, pylons, fence, detached coils or full switchyard.

One compact refinery fuel-tank module on a continuous rectangular raised service plinth: a squat vertical steel tank with heavily flaked dirty orange-rust paint, dark horizontal steel bands, a small top cap, tight yellow guardrail and short side ladder; one thick rust-red flanged pipe descends into a closed front pump cabinet, all physically connected within the footprint. A faded short 34 stencil on the tank, a bolted valve wheel and one amber caged maintenance lamp on the cabinet. Rough charcoal grime, wet dark metal, burnt yellow edge chips and deliberate ink contours from the refinery board. No live flames, spilled fuel, pipe network beyond the base, ground grating lane or complete refinery.

One long shallow closed ammunition-magazine bunker, flat low dark roof, thick dirty cream reinforced-concrete walls and chipped olive-grey steel corner plates. Two sealed heavy vertical-slatted roller shutters, a small side service door, a faded large but simple 37 stencil, warm amber entrance cage lamps and a single small dim red warning cage lamp. Heavy soot around vents, rusty hinges, old yellow loading-edge chips and coarse painted outlines from the munitions depot board. All lamps and roof hardware stay within the long narrow box. No ammunition crates, loose rounds, blast circles, forklift, military vehicle or whole armory compound.

One compact closed scrap-car compression press, a narrow tall rust-red and burnt-orange box frame with a toothed upper crosshead, a dark recessed but blocked compression mouth, thick side rails, one attached black cable winch drum and a few heavy chain loops pressed against the side. A continuous oil-stained lower steel plinth and one amber caged service lamp, faint dirty cream 10 stencil and worn black/yellow caution corners. Rough gouged metal, greasy deep charcoal shadows and chipped blue-grey panel repairs must match the scrap yard board. The compression mouth is stopped by a closed ram, not a traversable tunnel. No crushed-car stack, towing truck, crane, floor lane or workers.

One long narrow closed quarantine glasshouse bay, steep but low gabled roof carried by corroded charcoal steel mullions, dirty smoky blue-grey glazing with several boarded broken panes, and sparse olive ivy clinging to the frame. A closed end door, dim silhouettes of tightly packed plant trays only inside the structure, one short rusty water pipe and one small amber pendant lantern. Chipped pale green lower panels, dark moss at the sill, rough fracture edges and hand-painted ink outlines from the abandoned greenhouse board. Most glass must be cloudy and backed by dark interior planes so the footprint reads as a solid closed obstacle. No broad indoor garden, pathways, spore clouds, scientists or pots outside the footprint.

One closed storm-breakwater weather and beacon control station, a compact broad rectangle of salt-stained off-white steel and concrete, low flat black roof with rusty drip edges, two warm amber windows and a heavy shut service door. A short mast on the roof carries two small grey horn sensors, a compact dark wind sensor and a short red/cream windsock kept inside the outer footprint; a small amber roof beacon, chipped dark olive fittings and a faded 12 stencil. Use cold charcoal blue shadows, pitted grey surfaces, orange salt rust and bold weather-beaten ink contours from the breakwater reference. No ocean, waves, seawall, stairs, distant lighthouse, storm bolts or whole harbor.

One long straight industrial chain-link fence panel, three slender charcoal steel posts joined by top/bottom rails, rusty thin diamond wire mesh with true open holes, a restrained continuous barbed-wire strand on the top. Slightly bent battered posts, rubbed grey highlights and irregular ink-dark contours like board25 perimeter fencing. All post feet form a single narrow contact line and the complete structure stays in the depth envelope. No gate, sign, concrete wall, people, scenery or background-filled holes.

One damaged but still full-height compact civilian car, short boxy body, oxidized desaturated blue-grey paint with large old rust-red patches, dented hood and one crumpled door, cracked smoky windshield and four recognizable dark rubber wheels. Rough metallic chips, bent chrome trim, a dark but readable interior and strong painterly ink edges from board40 scrap cars. The footprint is compact, width58 depth112 totalheight27; retain a coherent body instead of a flat scrap pile. No stacked cars, tow truck, crane, loose detached doors, skid ground or police light bar.

One short industrial steel fuel barrel, circular width/depth30, totalheight25, heavily chipped rust-red paint, two dark raised steel hoops, a dented closed top with two bung caps, oily charcoal grime and a small faded cream hazard diamond. Preserve thick painterly dark contour, exposed orange metal scratches and wet matte metal from the reference, but no glossy toy sheen. Stable intact bottom rim, not a leaking or burning barrel. No flames, fuel puddle, smoke, multiple barrels or base tile.

One tall industrial amber worklamp: a slim dark charcoal post on a small circular bolted foot, an angular weathered steel support and a compact caged lantern head with warm dirty amber glass. Brass-grey rusted cage strips, an opaque dark cap, small cream highlights and a dim inner bulb. Lamp and any small handle stay within width/depth18 and totalheight80. Match the board19 foreground lamp and the amber caged lights across the mission references. No floodlight rig, generator, environment, exaggerated bloom, halo, hanging power cable, ground glow or floor base.
